national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has urged the private sector in space research to build a global aura of innovation so that people worldwide feel that if they want to make a career, they should go to India. Mr Modi stated this during an interaction with CEOs and founders of 20 space startups recently. According to the transcript of the interaction, which was released on National Space Day today, Prime Minister Modi also highlighted India’s cost-competitiveness in launching space ventures. During the interaction, Mr Modi urged the space sector startups to remain consistent in their efforts and build a robust space-sector ecosystem capable of attracting talent from across the world. During the interaction, Chief Executive Officer of India’s first space-tech unicorn, Skyroot Aerospace, Pawan Kumar Chandana thanked Mr Modi for opening up the space sector. He said that on 18th July, they successfully launched India’s first privately developed rocket. Meanwhile, National Space Day is being observed today. The country celebrates the day on 23rd of August every year to mark historic soft landing of Chandrayaan-3 near the Moon’s south pole, making India the first nation to reach the lunar south polar region. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended their greetings on the occasion. In a social media post, Mr Radhakrishnan said, India’s remarkable achievements in space exploration stand as a testament to country’s scientific excellence, spirit of innovation and determination to push the frontiers of knowledge. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while sharing a video on social media, said that in the new global order, India is continuously expanding its space sector. On National Space Day, Union Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh said the historic soft landing of Chandrayaan-3 placed India among the world’s leading spacefaring nations and lauded the remarkable contribution of the Indian scientists.

national_raw_news.title: 30 mins ago | National 139 Defence Minister Rajnath Singh stresses need for self-reliance in making warships, offshore vessels
national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today stressed the need for self-reliance in making warships, offshore vessels and in other related fields, describing it vital for security of the country. He emphasised the need for good-quality maintenance services in this field aimed at making India a future ship-building hub. Addressing the Bhumi Pujan ceremony for five projects of Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers (GRSE) and Yantra India Limited (YIL) in Kolkata worth approximately 3400 crore rupees, Mr Singh said Atmanirbharta is the need of the hour. He said GRSE could lead in future ship building. The Minister also informed GRSE is building a cargo ship for Germany. Emphasising the need to rely on the indigenous defence products, Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh today mentioned that the armed forces are now showing more interest in the products made by India’s defence public sector undertakings. West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari was present on the occasion. The minister said a growing vacuum in the shipbuilding sector worldwide can be captured by India under the “Make in India” campaign. To realise a Viksit Bharat by 2047, the contribution of GRSE and Yantra India Limited would be immense. Rajnath Singh also lauded the efforts of West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari for the state government’s co-operation to realise the aim of Vikshit Bharat by 2047. The minister said due care should be given to quality assurance and timely delivery of defence products for exports to the world. He mentioned that the armed forces are now relying on indigenous products for defence needs. Mr Singh said the State government is providing full cooperation in connection with internal security. He hoped the state would take steps to usher in a new renaissance of development with the launch of new projects. He mentioned that 11,000 acre lands have been provided by the state government for new projects. He said the Navratna company GRSE Limited has provided more than 100 vessels in recent times. The minister informed that YIL is not only providing traditional weapons but also research and development. Among the five projects, three projects of GRSE mark a significant step towards enhancing the shipyard’s manufacturing capacity and infrastructure. Advancing the Government of India’s Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India vision, these projects will enable the company to meet the growing requirements of the Maritime Forces and other defence and maritime stakeholders. The Bhumi Pujan ceremonies were conducted simultaneously at Kidderpore, Shalimar, Raichak and Ishapore across West Bengal.

national_raw_news.title: 32 mins ago | National 208 BRICS Sports Ministers adopt Joint Declaration in Visakhapatnam
national_raw_news.content: The BRICS Sports Ministers’ Meeting has successfully concluded in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, with the adoption of the BRICS Sports Joint Declaration by consensus. The meeting, held under India’s BRICS Chairship 2026, has given a fresh push to cooperation among BRICS countries in sports, with a focus on youth development, inclusion, sports technology and cultural exchange. A key outcome of the meeting has been the proposal to establish a BRICS Working Group on Sports Technology to promote cooperation in sports science, artificial intelligence, digital transformation and athlete performance. India’s proposal for a BRICS Sports Manufacturing Conclave has also received broad support. The inaugural conclave is proposed to be held in Udaipur in November this year, providing a platform for manufacturers, investors, technology companies and research institutions to share expertise and promote innovation. Another major initiative is the BRICS Traditional and Indigenous Sports Demonstration Games, proposed to be held in Ahmedabad in October. The event will showcase the rich sporting heritage of BRICS countries and strengthen cultural and people-to-people ties. Union Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya called for a BRICS Sporting Partnership that moves beyond declarations and leads to practical cooperation through athlete and coach exchanges, joint competitions and knowledge sharing. The successful BRICS Sports Ministers’ Meeting has laid the foundation for sustained sporting collaboration among BRICS nations.
